title: Add the provider-slot release transition to the scheduler authority kernel
description:
Objective: give `SLOT_STATES`' declared `RELEASED` member a transition that can reach it. Today no code path anywhere can move a provider slot to RELEASED, so `ExpansionReleaseEvidence.providerSlotState === "RELEASED"` is unreachable by construction and core's `safeRelease` predicate can never pass.

MEASURED GAP at HEAD a42ae2f.
- `packages/scheduler/src/authority/resource-model.ts:24` declares `SLOT_STATES = ["RESERVED", "ACTIVE", "RELEASED"]` and `ProviderSlotReservation {dimension, slotRef, requestId, state: SlotState, attemptRef}` (:82-88). Note `attemptRef` — the slot already carries its attempt edge, so nothing new has to be invented to bind a release to an attempt.
- `grep -rn "^export function" packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-resource.ts` returns `reserveAll`, `adapterConfirm`, `adapterFail`, `reserveProviderSlot` (:169), `activateProviderSlot` (:194), `grantSuccessorCapacity` (:222). There is NO release. `grep -rn "releaseProviderSlot|releaseSlot" packages/scheduler/src` returns ZERO.
- The ONLY `state: "RELEASED"` transition anywhere in packages/scheduler is `lease-drain.ts:223`, and that is the LEASE, not the slot.

So `RELEASED` is a member of a frozen vocabulary that nothing can produce. This is the mirror image of the usual defect: not a missing vocabulary entry, but a vocabulary entry with no producer.

CONTRAST WITH THE LEASE, which shows the shape to follow: `releaseWork` (lease-drain.ts:194) fences authority, refuses a malformed request, treats an already-RELEASED or REVOKED lease as `NO_OP` rather than an error, and returns `DRAINING` when the boundary is not yet settled and `RELEASED` when it is. A slot release wants the same three-way honesty, not a boolean.

Deliverable: a `releaseProviderSlot` transition in `packages/scheduler/src/authority/` returning the same `AuthorityOutcome` shape its siblings return, plus whatever re-export `packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-resource.ts` already does for `SLOT_STATES` and friends. Pure kernel only.

NOT in scope: the daemon composition that calls it (that is the lease/slot release composition task), the durable record, the expansion hold, or any reader.

Owned paths: the slot transition in packages/scheduler/src/authority/ plus its focused test. If the root export is required by a consumer, that is the consumer task's step, not this one — but do check `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts`, which today exports `SLOT_STATES` (:109) and the `LeaseState` type but NOT `LEASE_STATES`, `releaseWork`, `DrainDisposition`, `ReleaseHandoff`, `ReleaseRequest`, `ReleaseResult`, `applyDrainReason` or `parseDisposition` — all eight confirmed absent by a compiled bare-specifier probe that returned TS2305/TS2724 for each.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test — run the legs with exit codes captured separately and read the `Test Files N passed` count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: A provider slot can reach `RELEASED`: a test drives the new transition and asserts the returned reservation's `state` is `RELEASED`, where before the change no code path could produce that value.

The transition is THREE-WAY honest like its lease sibling, not a boolean: an already-RELEASED slot is a NO_OP rather than an error, a malformed request is refused with an exact code and layer, and a slot whose preconditions are unsettled does NOT silently release. Each arm pins its exact code and layer.
The transition refuses a release whose `attemptRef` does not match the reservation it names, with its own stable code — a slot released against the wrong attempt is authority leaking across attempts.
`SLOT_STATES` is consumed from its owning module, never retyped: a test asserts the transition's accepted inputs are exactly the frozen members, and a generated sweep asserts a positive case count.
A mutation that hardcodes the returned state to `RELEASED`, and separately one that drops the attemptRef check, each turn a NAMED test red; record both test names.

`pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` run with exit codes captured separately, the test leg prints a nonzero `Test Files N passed` count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Pure kernel only: no store, no clock, no filesystem, no daemon import. The scheduler decides transitions; persistence belongs to its consumer.

Follow the sibling `releaseWork` shape (lease-drain.ts:194) for outcome kinds and refusal discipline rather than inventing a fourth idiom in this package; reuse the existing AuthorityOutcome and refusal helpers.
Exact codes and layers on every refusal path, positive generated counts on any sweep, target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400.

implementationPlan.description: TDD, shape and identity refusals. Create `packages/scheduler/src/authority/provider-slot-release.test.ts` RED against a not-yet-written `releaseProviderSlot(predecessor, command)`. READ THIS FIRST, it determines how every arm must be written: this package's refusal helpers expose only TWO codes. `malformed(message)` emits `AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT` and `refuse(message)` emits `AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE` (authority-kernel.ts:207 and resource-model.ts, and `AuthorityErrorCode` is a CLOSED four-member union at authority-kernel.ts:79-81). Do NOT widen that union to give each refusal its own code — the sibling `activateProviderSlot` lives inside the same two, and a fifth member would ripple through the rejection-security record and the runtime error registry. Instead every refusal arm asserts the code AND the exact message string, because the message is the only discriminator available; a test pinning the code alone is one added guard away from vacuous. Arms: (a) a predecessor `parseProviderSlot` rejects (extra key, non-ref dimension/slotRef/requestId, a `state` outside `SLOT_STATES`, an `attemptRef` that is neither null nor a ref) -> AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT; (b) a malformed release command -> AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT; (c) a command whose `dimension`/`slotRef` do not match the reservation -> AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE with its own message; (d) a command naming a different `requestId` -> AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE with a DIFFERENT message. Assert (c) and (d) messages are not equal, or the two guards are indistinguishable.
implementationPlan.note: Created packages/scheduler/src/authority/provider-slot-release.test.ts RED against the not-yet-written releaseProviderSlot. Verified first: AuthorityErrorCode is a CLOSED 4-member union (authority-kernel.ts:79-81), malformed() always emits AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT (:207) and refuse() always emits AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE (resource-model.ts:212) — so the union is NOT widened and every refusal arm pins code AND exact message. Arms landed: (a) 25 malformed predecessor/command cases incl. extra key, symbol key, accessor, proxy, prototype-borrowed, state outside SLOT_STATES ("DRAINING"), attemptRef neither null nor ref; (b) command malformed cases in the same table; (c) dimension/slotRef drift -> AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE + IDENTITY_MESSAGE; (d) requestId drift -> AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE + a DIFFERENT message, and a dedicated test asserts all five messages are pairwise distinct (Set size === length) so no two guards are interchangeable. Fixtures seeded from production reserveAll -> reserveProviderSlot -> activateProviderSlot, never hand-transcribed. RED evidence: `npx vitest run --root . packages/scheduler/src/authority/provider-slot-release.test.ts` EXIT=1, "Cannot find module './provider-slot-release.js'", Test Files 1 failed (1).

implementationPlan.description: TDD, the attempt binding and the state machine, same test file. (e) THE ATTEMPT CHECK, which DoD 3 makes load-bearing: a release command whose `attemptRef` does not equal the reservation's `attemptRef` is refused with its own message — a slot released against the wrong attempt is authority leaking across attempts, and this is the mirror of `activateProviderSlot`'s existing `slot.attemptRef !== null` guard (lease-resource.ts:214). Include the null case explicitly: a reservation still at `RESERVED` with `attemptRef: null` has no attempt to release against and must refuse rather than treat null as a wildcard. (f) NO_OP, mirroring `releaseWork` (lease-drain.ts:199-201): a slot already in `RELEASED` returns an accepted no-op carrying the reservation unchanged, NOT a refusal — assert `ok` is true and every field is byte-equal to the input. (g) A slot in `RESERVED` (never activated) does not silently release; pin the exact message. (h) HAPPY PATH: an `ACTIVE` slot whose command matches on all four identities returns `ok` with `state === "RELEASED"`, and the test states plainly that before this change no code path in the repo could produce that value. (i) PURITY, matching the sibling's documented contract: the predecessor object is not mutated, not frozen, and not returned by reference — assert the returned record is a different object and that mutating the input afterwards does not change the result.
implementationPlan.note: Appended the attempt-binding and state-machine arms, still RED (EXIT=1, "Cannot find module './provider-slot-release.js'", Test Files 1 failed (1)). (e) attempt drift on an ACTIVE slot whose four identities otherwise match -> ATTEMPT_MESSAGE, so ONLY the attempt guard can answer; plus the explicit NULL sub-case — reservedSlot() is asserted to carry attemptRef === null before the call, proving null is refused rather than treated as a wildcard. (f) NO_OP built by releasing a real ACTIVE slot and REPLAYING the identical command against the successor: asserts ok true and toEqual(first.value), i.e. byte-equal, not a refusal. This forced a design decision recorded for the implementer: the successor KEEPS its attemptRef, otherwise the replay would hit the attempt guard (null vs ATTEMPT) and the NO_OP arm would be unreachable. (g) a RESERVED slot carrying attemptRef: ATTEMPT — identity AND attempt both match, so ONLY the state guard can refuse — pinned to stateMessage("RESERVED"); this is the reachability fix for the "refusal answered by an earlier guard" trap, since a naturally reserved slot has attemptRef null and would never reach the state check. (h) happy path asserts the full successor record with state "RELEASED" and Object.isFrozen. (i) purity: successor not the predecessor and not the command by reference, neither caller record frozen, JSON snapshot unchanged across the call, and a post-call mutation of the predecessor's attemptRef/state does not reach the returned value.

implementationPlan.description: TDD, the frozen-vocabulary sweep. Still in the same test file, drive `releaseProviderSlot` once per member of `SLOT_STATES` imported from `./resource-model.js` — never a locally retyped `["RESERVED","ACTIVE","RELEASED"]` literal, which is exactly the second-source-of-truth this sweep exists to prevent. Assert the outcome per state: RESERVED refuses, ACTIVE releases, RELEASED is the no-op. NON-VACUITY, and it is required by the epic rail: assert `SLOT_STATES.length === 3` and that the generated case list length equals it and is greater than zero, so a sweep that silently produced zero cases cannot pass. If a fourth member is ever added upstream the sweep must fail loudly rather than skip it.
implementationPlan.note: Added the frozen-vocabulary sweep, still RED (EXIT=1, module absent, Test Files 1 failed (1)). SLOT_STATES and SlotState are imported from their OWNING module ./resource-model.js — no local ["RESERVED","ACTIVE","RELEASED"] literal exists anywhere in the test file. Sweep 1 maps over SLOT_STATES to build one case per member, each carrying the matching attempt binding so `state` is the sole decider, and pins the disposition through an EXPECTED table typed Readonly<Record<SlotState, Disposition>> — exhaustive over the union, so a fourth upstream member makes tsc red as well. Non-vacuity assertions required by the epic rail: SLOT_STATES.length === 3, Object.keys(EXPECTED).length === SLOT_STATES.length, cases.length > 0, cases.length === SLOT_STATES.length, and cases.map(state) toEqual [...SLOT_STATES] so a silently-empty or reordered sweep cannot pass. Dispositions: RESERVED refuses with stateMessage("RESERVED"), ACTIVE releases to state "RELEASED" keeping attemptRef, RELEASED is the byte-equal no-op. Sweep 2 covers DoD 4's "accepted inputs are exactly the frozen members" from the other side: outsiders are GENERATED as [...LEASE_STATES, ...ACQUISITION_STATES] minus SLOT_STATES members (SUSPECT, DRAINING, REVOKED, PENDING_ACQUIRE, QUARANTINED), asserted length > 0 and duplicate-free, each refused AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT with the exact malformed message.

implementationPlan.description: Implement `packages/scheduler/src/authority/provider-slot-release.ts` plus its one-line bridge `provider-slot-release.js` — every sibling in `packages/scheduler/src/authority/` has one (authority-kernel.js, lease-drain.js, lease-fencing.js, lease-resource.js, lease-state.js, presence.js, resource-model.js) and they are git-tracked; without it the module is invisible at runtime while tsc and vitest both stay green. A NEW module rather than an addition to lease-resource.ts, which is at 238 of a 250-line target and would cross it. Reuse, do not reinvent: `parseProviderSlot` and `SLOT_STATES` from `./resource-model.js`, `accept` / `malformed` / `refuse` / `isRef` / `deepFreeze` from the same helpers the siblings use. Shape the command parser on `parseProviderSlotActivation` (resource-model.ts:200) — `exactRecord` over an explicit key tuple, every identity re-read from own data properties so an accessor, proxy or extra key cannot survive the parse. Return `AuthorityOutcome<ProviderSlotReservation>`. The successor is a FRESH frozen record built field by field, never a spread of the caller's object. Order the guards shape -> identity -> attempt binding -> state, so a malformed record can never reach the state check and be reported as a state problem.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
A NEW MODULE RATHER THAN AN ADDITION TO lease-resource.ts. That file already holds `reserveProviderSlot` (:169) and `activateProviderSlot` (:194), so it is the obvious home, but it is at 238 physical lines against a 250 target and a release transition with its own command parser lands around 35-45 lines. Adding it there crosses the target immediately and forces a split as collateral. A focused sibling module plus the existing re-export block gives consumers the same one-import experience without the split.

REFUSAL CODES: considered widening `AuthorityErrorCode` so each guard gets its own member, which is what the DoD's "its own stable code" reads like on first pass. Rejected on measurement: the union is a closed four-member type (authority-kernel.ts:79-81) and both refusal helpers are fixed — `malformed` always emits AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT and `refuse` always emits AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE. Its members feed `RejectionSecurityRecord` and the runtime error registry's safe-detail-key mapping, so a fifth member is a cross-package change far outside this task. The sibling transitions live inside the same two codes. The honest resolution is code-plus-message: every refusal arm pins both, and sibling arms assert their messages differ. That is the documented pattern for one-code-many-guards.

ROOT EXPORT: considered adding `releaseProviderSlot` to packages/scheduler/src/index.ts here. Rejected — the roster guards pin an exact export count and a sorted name list, and bumping them in a task whose consumer does not yet exist means the next task bumps them again. The consumer task task-8b2bb97b owns index.ts already.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD a42ae2f.

THE GAP IS REAL AND IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE USUAL ONE. `SLOT_STATES = ["RESERVED", "ACTIVE", "RELEASED"]` (resource-model.ts:24) declares a member that NOTHING can produce. `grep -rn "^export function" packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-resource.ts` returns reserveAll, adapterConfirm, adapterFail, reserveProviderSlot, activateProviderSlot, grantSuccessorCapacity — no release. `grep -rn "releaseProviderSlot|releaseSlot" packages/scheduler/src` returns ZERO. The only `state: "RELEASED"` transition in the whole package is lease-drain.ts:223, and that is the LEASE.

SHAPES. `ProviderSlotReservation {dimension, slotRef, requestId, state: SlotState, attemptRef: string | null}` (resource-model.ts:82-88). `parseProviderSlot` (:189) uses `exactRecord` over SLOT_KEYS, requires refs for dimension/slotRef/requestId, `oneOf(state, SLOT_STATES)`, and treats `attemptRef` as null-or-ref with an explicit comment that every other non-ref is malformed rather than "unbound". `parseProviderSlotActivation` (:200) is the command-parser template to copy.

OUTCOME AND HELPERS. `AuthorityOutcome<T> = {ok: true, value: T} | AuthorityRejection` (authority-kernel.ts:140). `AuthorityRejection {ok: false, issues: readonly AuthorityIssue[], securityRecord: RejectionSecurityRecord | null}` and `AuthorityIssue {code: AuthorityErrorCode, message: string}`. `accept` deep-freezes. So a test reads `refusal.issues[0].code` and `.message`; the existing suite already asserts `refusal.issues` has length 1 (index-surface.test.ts:989).

THE SIBLING TO MIRROR. `activateProviderSlot` (lease-resource.ts:194-219) is the exact template: parse both sides, `malformed` on either parse failure, then three separate `refuse` calls for dimension/slotRef mismatch, requestId mismatch and wrong state, then a guard that the slot is not already attempt-bound, then `accept(deepFreeze({...}))` built field by field. Its header states the purity contract explicitly — both inputs re-parsed from own data properties, fresh frozen successor, no caller record mutated, frozen or returned by reference — and this transition must satisfy the same.

THE LEASE SIBLING FOR OUTCOME SHAPE. `releaseWork` (lease-drain.ts:194) treats an already-RELEASED or REVOKED lease as an accepted NO_OP rather than an error, and splits DRAINING vs RELEASED on whether the boundary is settled. The slot has no drain concept, so the three-way honesty here is refuse-RESERVED / release-ACTIVE / no-op-RELEASED.

BRIDGES ARE MANDATORY. Every module in packages/scheduler/src/authority/ has a git-tracked one-line `.js` bridge: authority-kernel.js, lease-drain.js, lease-fencing.js, lease-resource.js, lease-state.js, presence.js, resource-model.js. A new .ts without one is invisible at runtime while tsc and vitest stay green.

ROSTER GUARDS EXIST HERE TOO. packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts pins `EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length` to 92 (:146) and a sorted-key equality (:251) — the same hand-transcribed two-axis shape as the runner's. Untouched by this plan by design.

GATE RESOLVES: `@moe/scheduler` is packages/scheduler with scripts typecheck and test.

FILE SIZES: lease-resource.ts 238, resource-model.ts 214, both near the 250 target.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE BIGGEST TRAP IS THE REFUSAL CODE. Only two codes are reachable and `refuse` gives all four identity/state guards the SAME one. A worker who writes `expect(issues[0].code).toBe("AUTHORITY_STALE_LEASE")` on every arm has written four copies of one assertion, and any single guard could be deleted with the suite staying green. Pin the message on every arm and assert sibling messages differ.
2. `attemptRef: null` is a legitimate parsed value, not an absence. A `RESERVED` slot has `attemptRef: null` by construction (reserveProviderSlot returns it that way), so a naive `slot.attemptRef === command.attemptRef` check must not treat null as a wildcard or as a match against a null command field. Refuse it explicitly and test it.
3. The NO_OP arm returns `ok: true`. A test written as "releasing twice refuses" will fail against the correct behaviour and may push a worker to change production instead of the test. The lease sibling already settled this question; follow it.
4. Do not widen `AuthorityErrorCode`. It is closed at four members and feeds `RejectionSecurityRecord` plus the runtime error registry's required safe-detail keys.
